title: Bonaventure — faith surer than sciences by adhesion, not speculation
source_text: XXXII. Ut scrupulus iste tollatur existimamus commode hic adhiberi posse distinctionem illam qua utitur Bonaventura inter Scholasticos Doctores percelebris. Nam comparans ille fidem cum scientiis quoad certitudinem, distinguit certitudinem, ut nos ante fecimus, in certitudinem cognitionis, seu speculationis, quae pertinet ad solum intellectum, & certitudinem adhaesionis, quae praecipue respicit voluntatem, & ab illa pendet. Dicitque fidem esse scientiis certiorem, non certitudine speculationis, seu certitudine solum adhaesionis. Quoniam, inquit ille, fideles Christiani nec argumentis, nec tormentis, neque blandimentis adduci possunt, vel inclinari, ut veritatem quam credunt, vel ore tenus negent: quod nemo peritus alicujus scientiae faceret, si acerrimis tormentis cogeretur sententiam suam de conclusione aliqua Geometrica, vel Arithmetica retractare. Stultus enim & ridiculus esset Geometra qui pro sua sententia in controversiis Geometricis mortem auderet subire, in quantum fides dictat non esse mentiendum.
pass_a_gloss: That this scruple may be removed we judge that that distinction may conveniently be employed here which Bonaventure, most celebrated among the Scholastic Doctors, uses. For comparing faith with the sciences as to certainty, he distinguishes certainty, as we did before, into certainty of cognition or speculation, which belongs to the intellect alone, and certainty of adhesion, which chiefly regards the will and depends on it. And he says that faith is more certain than the sciences, not by certainty of speculation, but only by certainty of adhesion. Because, he says, faithful Christians can be led or inclined neither by arguments nor by torments nor by blandishments to deny even with the mouth the truth they believe — which no one skilled in some science would do if by fiercest torments he were compelled to retract his opinion on some Geometric or Arithmetic conclusion. For a Geometer would be foolish and ridiculous who for his opinion in Geometric controversies would dare undergo death, inasmuch as faith dictates that one must not lie.
pass_b_english: Scruple-relief: Bonaventure’s cognition vs adhesion (as XIII).
Faith > sciences by adhesion-certainty, not speculation-certainty.
Martyr-cling vs geometer who won’t die for a theorem — faith forbids lying.
